body:
Looks reasonable to me. Some suggestions from claude:

<details><summary>AI review</summary>

Reviewed at ceb3c16. The SharedArrayBuffer refactor looks like it behaves the same as before: the order of the cross-origin isolation, `forStorage`, and deserialization checks hasn't changed. Lint passes; I didn't run a full build.

**Suggestions**
- `source:10501-10512`: in *restrict to the same agent cluster*, `forStorage` is optional and defaults to false. If another spec's serialization steps restrict `serialized` but forget to pass it, the restricted data can be stored (IndexedDB, history state) without an error. Consider making `forStorage` required. Alternatively, drop the argument and have *StructuredSerializeInternal* throw itself when `forStorage` is true and `serialized.[[AgentCluster]]` is non-null.
- *StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer*, step 3.1 (`source:11481`): the check runs inside the loop, so earlier holders' transfer-receiving steps have already run when it throws. For example, a `MessagePort` listed before a `[SameAgentCluster]` object gets entangled in `targetRealm` and then dropped. Consider checking every holder in a separate loop first. The existing "not exposed" check has the same problem, so maybe this is acceptable.
- PR description: the checklist is empty. Nothing in HTML uses `[SameAgentCluster]` yet, so I think tests and implementer interest would come with WebCodecs (w3c/webcodecs#717). Maybe say that in the PR.

**Nits**
- `source:10532-10535`: the *StructuredSerializeInternal* intro still says the result is always "realm-independent". It now needs the same "unless restricted" qualification the PR added to serialization steps.
- `source:10515-10517`: says Records created by *StructuredSerializeWithTransfer* have an [[AgentCluster]] field. Its return value ({ [[Serialized]], [[TransferDataHolders]] }) doesn't, only its transfer data holders do.

</details>

<details><summary>AI review</summary>
## Review of whatwg/html#13055 — "Allow restricting serialization and transfer to the same agent cluster" (head `2113e92`)

1. **`[Substantive]` The pre-pass in *StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer* only covers transfer data holders, not restricted records inside `[[Serialized]]`.**
   `postMessage(videoFrame, [port])` where `VideoFrame` is `[Serializable, SameAgentCluster]` (cloned, not transferred): the new loop passes (the port's holder has `[[AgentCluster]]: null`), the port is entangled in `targetRealm` via transfer-receiving steps, and only then does `? StructuredDeserialize([[Serialized]], …)` throw at the nested record — the port is lost exactly as before. This is pre-existing for the "not exposed" check, and the pre-pass is still an improvement for transferred `[SameAgentCluster]` objects, but as written it implies an atomicity it doesn't deliver. Either (a) add a note stating that restricted/unexposed *serialized* (non-transferred) values are still only detected during deserialization, or (b) go further and have *StructuredSerializeWithTransfer* record whether any record in the graph was restricted (e.g. a `[[AgentCluster]]` on the result that is the union, or a simple boolean), so the pre-pass can reject up front. (a) seems fine for this PR. `ALG-VALIDATE-BEFORE-SIDE-EFFECTS`

2. **`[Editorial]` Commit message vs. spec text on realm-independence.** The description says "A result restricted this way no longer needs to be realm-independent", but the normative text (correctly) keeps "must be independent of any realm" and *adds* "may also refer to data that is only accessible within that agent cluster". A restricted record still has to be deserializable in any realm of the cluster, so suggest the message say "…may additionally refer to data that is only accessible within that agent cluster."

3. **`[Editorial]` "Some serializable objects and transferable objects, such as `SharedArrayBuffer` objects…"** — per the dfn, *serializable objects* are platform objects with `[Serializable]`; SAB is a JS object "handled by StructuredSerialize directly". Suggest: "Some objects, such as `SharedArrayBuffer` objects, and some serializable objects and transferable objects, are restricted…" Relatedly, the *Serializable objects* intro ("…cloned across agent and even agent cluster boundaries", line 10274) is no longer universally true; a "generally" or a forward reference to the new section would square it.

4. **`[Editorial]` Declare the field where authors of serialization/transfer steps will look.** Nothing states that `serialized`/`dataHolder` carry an `[[AgentCluster]]` field (initially null) — the `restrict` hook just assigns to it. One sentence in the `<dt>`/`<dd>` for serialization steps and transfer steps (or in the new section) would make the contract explicit for other specs. `STATE-DECLARE`

5. **`[Nit]` Redundant two-step init.** "Set `serialized`.[[AgentCluster]] to null." immediately followed by "If `sameAgentCluster` is true, then restrict…" could be a single step: "If `sameAgentCluster` is true, then restrict `serialized`…; otherwise, set `serialized`.[[AgentCluster]] to null." Purely optional.
</details>

<details><summary>AI review</summary>

**Nits**
- `source:10515-10522` (base of the PR): the removed sentence saying StructuredDeserialize and StructuredDeserializeWithTransfer enforce the restriction would help specs migrate. mediacapture-extensions' own check (which uses `[[agentCluster]]`, lowercase, not HTML's field) is the kind of code it would remove. Consider restoring it in the new section.

</details>

When `MediaStreamTrack` adopts `[SameAgentCluster]`, the [transfer steps](https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-extensions/#transferable-mediastreamtrack) should drop setting `dataHolder.[[agentCluster]]` and the transfer-receiving steps should drop the agent cluster check. Otherwise there would be two checks.
Simon, I think that’s obvious and does not need specification language.
